name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,509

clue.text: Abrupt European national is scruffy individual

indicators.note: something abrupt is cut off short, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: a person from Slovenia

explanation.surface: A curt person from somewhere in Europe is dismissed as an untidy type.
explanation.definitionFit: A sloven is a person who is habitually careless and messy in appearance or habits.

clue.text: Gold blocks present in repository

indicators.note: something that blocks sits in the middle, obstructing the way through

blocks.note: or is gold in heraldry
to stage is to put on or present a show

explanation.surface: Gold bars sit in a vault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blocks' looks like gold bars but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Storage is a place where goods are kept, much as a repository is a store for things.

clue.text: Orange Republican in line for missile launchers

indicators.note: one part is placed inside the other

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for Republican
the oche is the line darts players stand behind

explanation.surface: A Republican in an orange tie queues behind rocket launchers.
explanation.walkthrough: The missiles are darts; the oche is the throwing line in a darts match.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy pigment ranging from yellow to brownish orange.

clue.text: Delight in predilection to go topless

indicators.note: in a down answer the top is the first letter, so going topless removes it

blocks.note: a strong liking

explanation.surface: Someone takes pleasure in a fondness for going topless.
explanation.definitionFit: To enchant someone is to charm or captivate them, filling them with pleasure.

clue.text: Lacking a natural ability to eat seconds

indicators.note: one part eats another, swallowing it so it ends up inside

blocks.note: taken as written
a bent is an aptitude or talent
S is the abbreviation for seconds

explanation.surface: Someone missing a born talent for eating second helpings.
explanation.walkthrough: S goes inside BENT, after A: A + BE(S)NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something absent is missing or not there, the same sense as wanting or being without.

clue.text: See what is written in heavy print

indicators.note: one thing written within another sits inside it

blocks.note: eh? is a request to repeat, as in what?
bold type is heavy print

explanation.surface: Look at the words printed in thick type.
explanation.definitionFit: Behold is an old-fashioned word meaning look at or observe.

clue.text: I say 'Reach out, and relax in this'

definitions.note: describes the noun by what you do in it

indicators.note: letters put out of place fall into a different order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone invites a guest to stretch out and unwind in a seat.
explanation.definitionFit: An easy chair is a large comfortable upholstered armchair made for lounging.

clue.text: Framework of report is enthralling rector

indicators.note: to enthral is to hold captive, so one part holds the other within

blocks.note: to tell is to report
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for rector

explanation.surface: An account of the structure is captivating the parish priest.
explanation.walkthrough: The rector's letter sits just after the first letter of the report word.
explanation.definitionFit: A trellis is a lattice of wooden or metal strips supporting climbing plants.

clue.text: Emergency stop crossing river - poor Declan is trapped

indicators.note: a poor version is spoilt, so the letters come out jumbled
something trapped is caught inside something else

blocks.note: the name's letters rearranged
fording is wading across a river

explanation.surface: Unlucky Declan is stuck midstream and has to halt urgently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Emergency stop' suggests a car braking, but the answer is an aircraft term.
explanation.definitionFit: A forced landing is an unplanned aircraft touchdown made because flight cannot safely continue.

clue.text: Parties hard to display money

blocks.note: dos are parties or celebrations
H for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Throwing lavish parties is a showy way of flaunting wealth.
explanation.walkthrough: Dosh is British slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Dosh is informal British slang for cash, so it stands for funds in general.

clue.text: Actor Earl breaks shoe in on-line clip?

indicators.note: to break into something is to force a way inside it

blocks.note: a wooden shoe
short for thespian
E is an abbreviation for earl

explanation.surface: A titled actor intrudes on a footwear deal made over the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On-line' is not the internet but a washing line, hence the question mark; thesp is informal for an actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A clothes peg is the little clip that holds wet laundry onto a washing line.

clue.text: Following hail, large area becomes slum

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
Latin greeting, as in Ave Maria
L for large, as in clothing sizes
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: After a hailstorm, a big district is reduced to a run-down neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: A favela is a Brazilian shanty town, an informal settlement of poor housing.

clue.text: Charlie getting on with order to produce ring, unexpectedly

blocks.note: Charlie is C in the radio alphabet
someone getting on is ageing
a call can be a summons or command

explanation.surface: Charlie, ageing, demands that a jeweller produce a ring, out of the blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like jewellery but is the verb to telephone.
explanation.definitionFit: To cold call is to telephone someone uninvited, typically a sales pitch they were not expecting.

clue.text: Get away with cuddle, oddly lacking happiness

indicators.note: the letters in odd positions are missing, leaving only the even ones

blocks.note: slang command to go away
second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Told to clear off with no hug, someone ends up short of joy.
explanation.definitionFit: Beatitude is a state of supreme blessedness, utmost bliss or contentment.

clue.text: Proposes key food additive

blocks.note: to table a motion is to propose it, in British usage
the Alt key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: A committee member puts forward a crucial flavour enhancer.
explanation.definitionFit: Table salt is fine sodium chloride sprinkled on or added to meals for seasoning.

clue.text: Supports ecstasy being taken in pubs

indicators.note: the drug is taken away, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: bears as in holds up
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone backs ecstasy use in drinking places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken' suggests drug-taking, but here it means removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Bars are drinking establishments, the same places as public houses or taverns.

clue.text: See live part of brain

blocks.note: lo, an old word meaning look
to be is to exist

explanation.surface: Watching a live scan of a section of the brain.
explanation.definitionFit: The cerebrum is divided into lobes, rounded sections such as the frontal and temporal.

clue.text: Poles pursue the Parisian around Paris, primarily providing protection for photographer

indicators.note: things that pursue come after, so they follow in the answer
primarily means first, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: le is French for the
north and south, the two poles
ca, short for circa, means around
the city's opening letter

explanation.surface: Polish paparazzi tail a French figure through the city, hounding the press photographer.
explanation.definitionFit: A lens cap is a cover clipped over a camera lens to shield the glass from scratches and dust.

clue.text: Jumping bail, in case judge factors in readings

indicators.note: the letters jump about into a new order
one part is placed inside the other

blocks.note: the letters rearranged
a packing case

explanation.surface: A defendant who skips bail lets the judge weigh the case accordingly.
explanation.walkthrough: The scrambled letters go inside CRATE after its C. 'Judge' looks like the court official but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To calibrate an instrument is to assess and correct the scale it displays against a standard.

clue.text: Be left at home by husband, with weary back

indicators.note: going back means reading the word from end to start

blocks.note: in means at home
H is the abbreviation for husband
tire as in grow weary

explanation.surface: A wife is left at home by her husband, who returns exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be left' is the passive sense: to be left something in a will.
explanation.definitionFit: To inherit is to receive property or money bequeathed under someone's will after their death.

clue.text: Eliot concealing difficult low periods

indicators.note: to conceal is to hide inside, so one part goes within the other

blocks.note: the poet T. S. Eliot's initials
rough as in hard going

explanation.surface: The poet hid his years of struggle and depression.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface fits T. S. Eliot, who wrote through depression.
explanation.definitionFit: Troughs are low points in a cycle, such as slumps in an economy or in one's mood.

clue.text: Screen question prior to opening of enquiry

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: to grill is to interrogate
the word's first letter

explanation.surface: Vetting candidates by quizzing them before an inquiry opens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screen' looks like a verb, to vet, but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A grille is a grating or lattice of bars set across an opening as a barrier or partition.

clue.text: Caused to be loved as death approached, an unspecified number lost

indicators.note: something lost is missing from what remains

blocks.note: death is the end
came close to
N is the algebraic symbol for any number

explanation.surface: As the end drew near, someone became cherished, though many had gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Endeared means made dear to someone, winning their affection or fondness.

clue.text: Associate reported control switch for stove?

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so it is heard rather than read

blocks.note: a knob on a hob, the cooking surface

explanation.surface: A colleague mentions the dial that turns the cooker on.
explanation.definitionFit: To hobnob is to mix socially, especially with people of higher status.

clue.text: Best to eat large carp

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so one part swallows the other

blocks.note: to best someone is to beat them
L for large, as in clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Advice on whether a big fish is good to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carp' looks like the fish but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To bleat is to complain in a whining, feeble way, just as carping is persistent grumbling.

clue.text: Reliance on unstable ship

indicators.note: unstable letters will not stay put and fall into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Depending on a vessel that is not seaworthy.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocean liner is a large passenger vessel built to cross open seas on a regular route.

clue.text: So I must welcome king

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so one part holds the other inside

blocks.note: ego is Latin for I, the self
R for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Someone resigned to having to greet the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergo is Latin for therefore, used to introduce a logical conclusion.

clue.text: Club for Green Party leader, say

blocks.note: first meaning: the golf club used on the green
second meaning: a player taking strokes on the green, playfully cast as a party chief

explanation.surface: A political club naming the head of an environmentalist party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green Party' is not politics: the green is the short-grass area round a golf hole.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer uses this flat-faced iron on the green, and anyone tapping the ball there is one too.

clue.text: Data about university's ranking

indicators.note: about means going round, so one part surrounds the other

blocks.note: short for statistics
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Figures concerning a college's league table position.
explanation.definitionFit: Status is relative standing or position in a hierarchy, the same idea as one's rank.
